headline: Runtime and memory efficiency in microbial genomic and metagenomic software tools
label: Microbial Genomics Software Tools
summary: Recent preprints and papers report runtime and memory footprints alongside accuracy for microbial genomics and metagenomics tools.
synthesis: The common thread is the evaluation and engineering of computational tools for microbial genomic and metagenomic analysis, with computational cost treated alongside accuracy. A native Python ANCOM-BC implementation in scikit-bio reports a 100-fold runtime speedup and 87% memory reduction relative to the R implementation for compositional differential abundance testing. MAT-classifier targets genus-level profiling of ancient metagenomic data and outperforms aMeta in simulated accuracy. ViralClust packages five clustering algorithms in a Nextflow pipeline to select bias-aware representative viral genomes. A benchmark of seven Hi-C read-alignment strategies identifies BWA MEM -5SP as yielding the most inter-contig pairs. A PCR bias study finds Shannon and Weighted UniFrac sensitive to amplification effects. What is new is the joint reporting of resource use with accuracy and benchmarked method choice, although the items differ in scope and not all report resource metrics.
